title: Model-flagged kernel profiles and rollback safety net for heterogeneous architectures
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a model-onboard flow that consumes model-provided architecture flags (e.g., MHA/GQA/MoE hints) to select a pinned kernel profile during publishing, with an automated rollback safety-net and staged rollout. The goal is to reduce manual compiler tuning for common edge-case architectures while keeping a low-risk path when performance or correctness regressions are detected.
background: We currently require manual engineering intervention to pick kernel bundles and compile profiles for incoming models that use nonstandard attention patterns (GQA, MoE, grouped attention). This leads to onboarding delays and reactive patches when a pinned profile produces regression. Product asks for faster time-to-serve and predictable SLOs for Dedicated/Private customers.
design_decisions: Models may include a metadata field 'redwood_arch_flags' containing standardized tokens (e.g., 'MHA_V2', 'GQA_SPLIT=8', 'MoE_SHARDING=expert-2'). These flags are advisory, not authoritative.
Onboarder will use a ruleset to map flags to a candidate kernel profile (compile bundle id) and a fallback profile list ordered by risk/cost.
Pinning occurs at model-version publish time; initial pin is labeled 'candidate' and placed into a staged rollout targeting 10% of traffic, with progressive increase based on telemetry.

Rollback safety net: if telemetry signals (latency p95 increase > 20% or token-error-rate > 0.2%) within a 30-minute window for the canary cohort, system auto-fails over to the next fallback profile and demotes the candidate.
Human-in-the-loop: an oncall alert routes to runtime/infra owners with a runbook; engineers can override auto-fallback and mark a profile as quarantined.
Telemetry events and deterministic hashes used to ensure canary populations are stable and reproducible across regions for A/B comparisons.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarder parses 'redwood_arch_flags' from model metadata and selects a candidate kernel profile automatically for MHA/GQA/MoE variants.
Publishing a model-version with candidate pin creates a staged rollout record and traffic split config (10% canary by default).
Runtime emits telemetry events for candidate vs baseline including p50/p95 latency, token throughput, and correctness regression signals (nan-check, logits-shift metric).
Auto-fallback triggers within 30 minutes when configured thresholds are exceeded and traffic for canary switches to fallback profile without dropping requests.
Documentation and runbook published in Confluence with PR links to onboarding ruleset and mapping table.
E2E tests simulate MHA/GQA/MoE patterns and validate compilation selection, fallback, and rollback behavior in CI (mock runtime).
tasks: Define canonical 'redwood_arch_flags' token set and schema; write parser in model-onboarder (Aisha)
Implement mapping ruleset service: flags -> candidate profile + fallback chain (Marco)
Extend publish API to support 'candidate' pin label and staged rollout record (Backend)
Runtime: add canary routing switch and safe-fallback API (Runtime team)
Telemetry: add candidate/baseline tags and implement regression detectors (Telemetry/Observability)
Oncall/runbook and alerting thresholds; define mitigation steps (SRE)
Add CI tests for simulated MoE/GQA/MHA compile + canary failure -> auto-fallback (QA)
